Pros:
AWD by default — 4 motors drive each corner independently, maximizing torque delivery and eliminating belt tension asymmetry
Gantry geometry is engineered around Input Shaper optimization — resonance peaks are higher than any 2020 2-motor CoreXY
Minimum moving mass — every component choice trades weight against stiffness in favor of lower inertia
Open source — all design files on GitHub; community has documented full builds
Description: The VzBot AWD gantry is the defining component of the VzBot ecosystem — a 4-motor CoreXY (AWD) gantry on 2020 extrusion, engineered from the ground up for high-acceleration Klipper printing. Every geometry decision exists to minimize mass and maximize resonance frequency. AWD is not an optional feature; it is the VzBot’s core identity.
Verdict Label: Purpose-built for maximum acceleration — AWD 4-motor gantry with minimum moving mass and optimized belt geometry
Cons:
Expert-level build — AWD gantry assembly requires precise alignment of 4 motor positions
Klipper hybrid_corexy configuration required — not plug-and-play with standard CoreXY configs
Not enclosed by default — high acceleration builds with open frames have thermal consistency trade-offs
Very small community relative to Voron — fewer documented build references
Name: VzBot AWD Gantry

Pros:
Corrects the asymmetric belt path geometry in the stock V2.4 gantry — documented improvement in motion linearity
Improved idler tower geometry reduces the flex that limits stock acceleration
Open source, community-maintained, well-documented upgrade path from stock
Highly compatible — uses the same extrusion size and motor positions as stock
Description: The Pandora Gantry is a community-designed replacement for the Voron 2.4 stock XY gantry that addresses the stock design’s belt geometry asymmetry and idler tower rigidity. It is the most widely adopted V2.4 gantry upgrade in the Voron community — with extensive build documentation and Input Shaper comparison data available. New printed parts are required; extrusion and motors remain from stock.
Verdict Label: The community’s most-recommended V2.4 gantry upgrade — corrects stock belt geometry and adds measurable rigidity
Cons:
Not a drop-in replacement — requires reprinting motor mounts and idler towers
Still uses 2020 extrusion; for maximum rigidity, Titanium Backers are a complementary follow-on
Installation requires full gantry disassembly and belt re-routing
Name: Pandora Gantry

Pros:
Designed around dimensional accuracy and repeatability — the gantry geometry prioritizes motion linearity over maximum acceleration
Kinematic design reduces accumulated positioning error — suited for precision engineering parts
Open source — all design files on GitHub
Fully enclosed by design — thermal consistency is built into the platform architecture
Description: The HevORT HRE gantry is a 2020/2040 aluminum extrusion CoreXY gantry designed for dimensional precision and repeatability. Unlike VzBot (which optimizes for speed) or Voron (which optimizes for community ecosystem), HevORT’s gantry prioritizes motion linearity and long-term positional accuracy. The community is small and primarily European; this is not a gantry for builders new to self-build.
Verdict Label: Precision-first CoreXY gantry — engineered for dimensional accuracy and repeatability over speed, small community
Cons:
Very small community — limited build documentation, fewer reference builds to compare against
No kit available — self-sourcing all gantry components is required, often from European vendors
Not optimized for speed — if print rate is the priority, VzBot or RatRig V-Core 4 are better choices
Firmware tuning resources are sparse relative to Voron or RatRig
Name: HevORT HRE Gantry

Pros:
Fully documented on vorondesign.com — build guides, CAD, and Klipper configs all assume this gantry
Well-understood failure modes and tuning strategies — the community has years of Input Shaper data for this specific design
Direct CAD and BOM integration — no compatibility guesswork
Description: The Voron 2.4 stock gantry is a 2020 aluminum extrusion CoreXY with 2 XY motors and printed idler towers and motor mounts. It works well out of the box and is the baseline all V2.4 documentation assumes. The community has iterated significantly on it; aftermarket upgrades like Pandora and Titanium Backers address its main limitations.
Verdict Label: Functional baseline — community consistently upgrades it, but it works and the documentation is thorough
Cons:
Belt geometry is not perfectly symmetric in the stock design — community mods (Pandora, Archetype) address this
Aluminum extrusion flex at temperature is meaningful — Titanium Backers are a common follow-on upgrade
4-hole idler towers are a known weak point at high acceleration
Name: Voron 2.4 Stock Gantry

Pros:
1515 extrusion keeps mass low — the 0.2 gantry is inherently lighter than any 2020 design
No significant community demand to upgrade it — the stock design is well-regarded for its size class
Fully documented; same Voron community support as full-size variants
Description: The Voron 0.2 mini gantry uses 1515 aluminum extrusion rather than the 2020 used in V2.4 and Trident — appropriate for the 120mm build volume where 2020 would add unnecessary mass. The design is considered well-matched to the printer’s scale, and unlike the full-size Voron gantries, the community has not produced significant aftermarket alternatives.
Verdict Label: Well-engineered compact gantry — 1515 extrusion scales the CoreXY design correctly to the 0.2’s 120mm build volume
Cons:
1515 extrusion is harder to source than 2020 — Misumi and LDO are primary vendors
1515 is less rigid per unit length than 2020 — but the short span of a 120mm gantry makes this a non-issue in practice
Printed idler towers on a small gantry require careful assembly for belt tension consistency
Name: Voron 0.2 Mini Gantry

Pros:
Eliminates gantry bow caused by differential thermal expansion between aluminum extrusion and steel linear rails — a real and measurable print quality issue at chamber temp
Titanium’s coefficient of thermal expansion closely matches the linear rail steel — this is why titanium specifically, not aluminum
Sold pre-cut by Fabreeko, KB3D, and others — hardware-only installation, no printing required
Widely considered mandatory by experienced V2.4 builders running enclosed hot chambers
Description: Titanium Backers are thin strips of titanium inserted between the gantry’s MGN12H linear rails and the 2020 extrusion. Aluminum expands more with heat than steel rails, which causes the gantry to bow at chamber temperature and introduces first-layer errors. Titanium’s expansion rate is close enough to steel to prevent this. Considered one of the most impactful V2.4 and Trident upgrades per dollar.
Verdict Label: The single most cost-effective V2.4 and Trident upgrade — titanium strips that eliminate gantry bow from thermal expansion
Cons:
Not a drop-in — requires removing linear rails from the extrusion, inserting backers, and reinstalling
Not cheap for what they are — but the price is justified by the improvement
Stainless steel backers exist as a budget alternative but have slightly worse thermal expansion match than titanium
Name: Titanium Backers

Pros:
3030 extrusion is substantially stiffer than 2020 — belt geometry and gantry rigidity are better at the same span length
AWD (4-motor) XY drive eliminates conventional CoreXY belt tension asymmetry — each corner is independently driven
IDEX-capable by design — the gantry supports dual carriages without modification
Official RatRig product — engineered and tested rather than community-iterated
No aftermarket gantry upgrade needed — the stock gantry is the community benchmark
Description: The RatRig V-Core 4 gantry is the stock AWD CoreXY gantry of the V-Core 4 — a 3030 aluminum extrusion frame with 4 independent XY stepper motors (one per corner). AWD eliminates belt tension asymmetry, the 3030 extrusion provides exceptional rigidity, and IDEX dual-carriage operation is supported by the gantry design without modification. It is the most mechanically refined stock gantry in the prosumer self-build ecosystem.
Verdict Label: Most refined stock gantry in the prosumer ecosystem — 3030 extrusion, 4-motor AWD, and IDEX-capable by design
Cons:
3030 extrusion is more expensive and harder to source than 2020 — not a DIY-compatible upgrade path
AWD requires 4 stepper drivers and correct firmware configuration (Klipper hybrid_corexy)
3030 gantry is heavier than 2020 equivalents — the tradeoff for rigidity is moving mass
Name: RatRig V-Core 4 Gantry

Pros:
Fixed gantry — the XY frame never moves in Z, which eliminates a whole class of gantry mass and resonance issues vs V2.4
Same documentation and community support as V2.4 — all Voron tuning resources apply
Compatible with the same toolhead ecosystem as V2.4
Description: The Voron Trident stock gantry is a fixed-in-Z 2020 extrusion CoreXY — unlike the V2.4, the gantry doesn’t move during printing, which reduces one source of resonance. It uses the same 2-motor XY motion, printed idler towers, and belt routing as the V2.4 with the same community-documented limitations.
Verdict Label: Solid fixed gantry — simpler than V2.4 because it never moves in Z, but same belt geometry limitations apply
Cons:
Same belt geometry limitations as V2.4 stock gantry — idler positioning is not optimally symmetric
Titanium Backers are still a recommended follow-on for the same thermal expansion reasons as V2.4
Printed idler towers are the same weak point as V2.4 at high acceleration
Name: Voron Trident Stock Gantry

Pros:
Designed around reducing gantry moving mass — lower resonance peaks allow higher Input Shaper acceleration limits
Open source community project with documented performance improvements
Compatible with V2.4 extrusion and motor positions — reuses existing hardware
Description: The Archetype Gantry is a community-designed Voron 2.4 gantry upgrade that prioritizes reduction in moving mass to push Input Shaper resonance peaks higher. Where the Pandora focuses on geometry correction and rigidity, the Archetype trades some of that rigidity for lighter printed components — the tradeoff that makes sense for builders chasing maximum acceleration.
Verdict Label: Lightweight performance-oriented V2.4 gantry upgrade — prioritizes mass reduction for higher acceleration headroom
Cons:
Not a drop-in replacement — requires new printed parts and full gantry teardown
Mass reduction focus means some structural compromises vs heavier reinforced alternatives like Pandora
Smaller builder base than Pandora — fewer documented builds to reference during installation
Name: Archetype Gantry
